name: WeChat Work
description: WeChat Work, now branded WeCom, is Tencent's enterprise communication and collaboration platform for organizations, members, applications, messaging, contacts, and events.
agentUseSummary: WeChat Work cannot currently be connected because the candidate does not identify one safe provider-native product. Third-party member authorization omits a real display name and fails Relay's useful-read bar, while enterprise installation gives a reviewed service-provider suite a permanent corporation delegation, application-agent authority, visible-member privileges, and encrypted callback obligations broader than a narrow read wrapper.

blocked.label: Connect member identity
blocked.description: Third-party member authorization returns opaque corporation/member identifiers and does not provide the member's real name, so it does not meet Relay's useful profile-read contract.

blocked.label: Inspect enterprise authorization
blocked.description: A useful corporation/application inspection would retain a permanent service-provider suite delegation and application-agent authority broader than the proposed read wrapper.

blocked.label: Use application messaging or events
blocked.description: Messaging and event ingestion require a separate recipient, callback, retention, approval, anti-spam, licensing, and disconnect product decision.

blocked.label: Access contacts or administration
blocked.description: Directory visibility and contact read/write privileges are privacy-sensitive administrative authority and are not approved for this collaboration candidate.

blocked.label: Use raw WeCom access
blocked.description: Raw endpoints, suite tokens, permanent codes, corporation tokens, arbitrary API calls, exports, and every unspecified read or write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action can be enabled until Relay selects one exact WeCom product and accepts its provider-specific authority, privacy, callback, retention, licensing, and revocation contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No WeChat Work product surface or wrapper contract is authorized to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No WeChat Work product surface or wrapper contract is authorized to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Member authorization is not a useful name-bearing profile read, while enterprise suite authorization carries permanent corporation/application authority broader than a narrow wrapper; the candidate does not choose identity, authorization inspection, messaging/events, or contacts administration.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials or show Connect. Reconsider only after an explicit product decision selects one exact provider-native surface and accepts its suite authority, callback, privacy, retention, licensing, and cancellation-deletion obligations.

evidence.supports: WeCom documents third-party member authorization returning corporation/member identifiers and a conditional user ticket rather than a conventional durable delegated account grant.
WeCom's third-party member read contract substitutes the member identifier for the real member name, preventing a useful name-bearing Relay profile result.
The service-provider lifecycle derives a short-lived suite access token from Suite ID, Suite Secret, and the latest callback-delivered Suite Ticket.
Enterprise installation exchanges a one-time authorization code for a permanent per-corporation delegation rather than a narrow user OAuth token.
Third-party applications must process signed and encrypted create, change, and cancellation authorization callbacks and reconcile or delete corporation state.
